chapter_title: Day 8: Rhodes, From the Colossus to the Knights
learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of nine olive oil labels supports the claim on its front, using the EU grade limits, the cold-extraction rule, harvest dates, and origin wording, judging at least 7 of 9 correctly on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** read-the-olive-oil-label
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of nine olive oil labels supports the claim on its front, using the EU grade limits, the cold-extraction rule, harvest dates, and origin wording, judging at least 7 of 9 correctly on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** olive oil, the four grades and their free-acidity limits, malaxation, cold extraction below 27 °C, harvest date versus best-before date, calories per tablespoon (all defined in the section "Olive Oil" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each label, the learner chooses "Supports the claim" or "Does not support the claim" before feedback. A judgment is correct when it matches the Correct judgment column in Content. Mastery is 7 of 9 correct on the first attempt. **Misconceptions:** (1) "Light" olive oil has fewer calories (label 2). (2) Any oil called extra virgin is extra virgin, whatever its acidity (label 3). (3) "Cold" is a vague marketing word with no rule (labels 4 and 5). (4) A blend containing virgin oil can be called extra virgin (label 6). (5) A best-before date in the future means the oil is fresh (label 7). (6) An oil bottled or sold in Greece is Greek oil (label 8). **Instructional Rationale:** Judging a claim against evidence on the same label is an Evaluate task: the learner applies a standard to decide whether a claim is justified. Pairing a supported and an unsupported "cold extraction" label, and including three labels that do support their claims, keeps the learner from simply rejecting every marketing phrase. **Content:** Each label shows the front claim and the back-label details. | # | Front claim | Back-label details | Correct judgment | Reason shown after answering | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | "Fresh extra virgin olive oil" | Extra virgin; harvest 2026/27; acidity ≤ 0.3%; dark glass | Supports the claim | Acidity is well under the 0.8% limit, and the harvest is this season's. | | 2 | "Light olive oil: fewer calories!" | Olive oil composed of refined olive oils and virgin olive oils; 120 kcal per tablespoon | Does not support the claim | "Light" means mild flavor and pale color; every oil has about 120 calories per tablespoon. | | 3 | "Extra virgin olive oil" | Acidity 1.5% | Does not support the claim | Extra virgin requires free acidity of 0.8% or less; 1.5% is at best virgin. | | 4 | "Cold extraction" | Extra virgin; malaxation and extraction at 25 °C | Supports the claim | EU rules allow "cold extraction" when the oil is kept below 27 °C, and 25 °C is below it. | | 5 | "Cold extraction" | Extra virgin; extraction at 32 °C | Does not support the claim | 32 °C is above the 27 °C limit for the words "cold extraction." | | 6 | "Extra virgin olive oil" | Ingredients: refined olive oils and virgin olive oils | Does not support the claim | A blend of refined and virgin oils is the grade "olive oil," not extra virgin. | | 7 | "This season's oil" (bought in November 2026) | Extra virgin; harvest 2024/25; best before December 2026 | Does not support the claim | The oil is two harvests old; the best-before date does not make it this season's. | | 8 | "Greek olive oil" | Extra virgin; blend of olive oils of European Union origin; bottled in Greece | Does not support the claim | "Blend of EU oils" can mean oil from several countries; bottling in Greece does not make it Greek oil. | | 9 | "Early-harvest green oil" (*agourélaio*) | Extra virgin; harvest October 2026; product of Greece | Supports the claim | An October harvest is early in the season, and the origin is stated as Greece. | **Provenance:** Grade names and free-acidity limits (extra virgin 0.8% or less; virgin 2.0% or less; refined-and-virgin blend 1.0% or less; lampante above 2.0%), the 27 °C condition for "cold extraction," and the origin wording "blend of olive oils of European Union origin" are from the EU marketing standards for olive oil, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/2104; the generator must check each value against that regulation and flag any difference to the author. The calorie value (about 120 kcal per tablespoon) is from the USDA FoodData Central entry for olive oil. The nine labels are illustrative and must be labeled "Illustrative labels" in the sim. **Rules:** Each label is answered once for scoring. A first-attempt judgment is correct if and only if it equals the Correct judgment. Score is 0 to 9. Mastery is score >= 7. Labels are shown in the fixed order 1 to 9. Thresholds: extra virgin requires acidity <= 0.8%; "cold extraction" requires temperature < 27 °C. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the claim on the front of label 1, then turns the label to read the back. 2. The learner chooses "Supports the claim" or "Does not support the claim." 3. Feedback appears, with the back-label detail that decides the case marked. 4. The learner repeats for labels 2 to 9. 5. After label 9, the learner sees a summary: 3 labels support their claims, 6 do not, with their own score. 6. The learner should notice that the deciding facts were always on the back label, in the acidity, the temperature, the ingredients, the harvest date, or the origin line. **Feedback:** Nine labels, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: ." Incorrect: "Look again: ." A running score "Labels judged correctly: n of 9" is shown. At the end: if score >= 7, "You can read an olive oil label like a Greek grandmother."; otherwise, "Check the back label first: acidity, temperature, ingredients, harvest, origin." A Try Again option repeats all nine labels. **Starting State:** Label 1 showing its front claim, a button to turn it over, the two judgment choices, and the question "Does the bottle live up to its claim?" **Chapter Anchors:** Extra virgin 0.8% or less; virgin 2.0% or less; refined-and-virgin blend 1.0% or less; lampante above 2.0%; cold extraction below 27 °C; about 120 calories per tablespoon; harvest from October to January; nine labels; three support their claims; mastery 7 of 9.
